In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CGRP expression in mixed and pure IDC is a marker of aggressiveness, and it is associated with stromal involvement.
CGRP is an indicator of breast cancer aggressiveness, and its expression is significantly increased in IDC + DCIS as compared with pure IDC.
IDC + DCIS is a more aggressive disease than pure IDC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the higher BD, SMM uptake, and Ki- 67, the lower the ER and the more CGRP-positive the tumor, the higher the probability that the lesion will be a mixed IDC +  DCIS.
CGRP expression is increased in IDC + DCIS and in grade II IDC, and this may be associated with a higher proliferative activity and ER-independent pathway.
IDC +DCIS is a more aggressive entity than pure IDC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CGRP is a promising marker for the evaluation of tumor aggressiveness, especially in IDC +DCIS.
CGRP is associated with a higher proliferation rate, a lower BD, and a higher SMM in patients with IDC +  DCIS.
CGRP may be a useful marker for the identification of IDC + IDC patients with high risk of recurrence and poor prognosis.
